A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same O’CLOK-UCB research despite the changed title and terminology. Their complete main texts, figures, table, equations, and Appendix A proofs are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original movie-recommendation, crowdsourcing, and synthetic simulations, including reward, regret, and runtime results in Figures 2–7.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original simulations and their reported reward, regret, and runtime results in Figures 2–7.

M1.justification: The GP posterior updates, UCB indices, oracle selection, and sparse approximation procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 moves index computation inside the per-arm loop, which is procedurally equivalent.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MovieLens 25M recommendation, Tokyo Foursquare crowdsourcing, and synthetic varying arm codependency. V2 adds shortest-path and stochastic-ranking examples in Sections 2.3.4–2.3.5, but does not evaluate them.

E2.justification: The actual comparisons retain ACC-UCB in Simulation I and ACC-UCB plus CC-MAB in Simulations II–III, alongside the same oracle benchmarks and full/sparse GP variants. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The simulations retain their preprocessing, arm-arrival distributions, round budgets, reward functions, kernel settings, inducing-point configurations, and evaluation metrics. No new experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The inducing-point sensitivity comparisons and Simulation III’s five kernel-lengthscale conditions are retained with the same evidence. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repetitions for the simulations, with standard-deviation error bars explicitly described for Simulations II and III. The uncertainty displays and reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–7 retain the same plotted results, rankings, uncertainty displays, and runtime curves. The corresponding numerical comparisons and qualitative experimental findings in Section 5 are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A substantially revises Lemma 3 from a 1/K-weighted logarithmic variance bound to an eigenvalue-and-trace bound, changing Theorem 1’s regret guarantee. V2 also replaces the earlier fixed-cardinality analysis with revised information-gain statements and Corollary 1 using the total number of selected arms, and changes the kernel-specific bounds. These are substantive mathematical revisions beyond renumbering; the GP covariance definition is also corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions replace the explicit K factor in the regret guarantee with sqrt(λ*(K)K) and emphasize an improved independent-arm case. The empirical superiority claims remain. Section 6 additionally states a bound without the eigenvalue factor or the independent-arm qualification.

C2.justification: Remark 1 adds an explanation of covariance-dependent regret and the diagonal-covariance special case. Section 6 newly identifies oracle access and the Lipschitz requirement as limitations and acknowledges uncertainty about tightness in K. Experimental interpretations and the existing future-research proposal are retained.

D1.justification: The reported hardware, Python/GPflow implementation, hyperparameters, inducing-point selection procedure, data processing, and source-code/preprocessed-data access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 broadens the combinatorial-bandit background with citations on pure exploration, matroid bandits, cascading bandits, and probabilistically triggered arms, and adds references supporting ranking and eigenvalue discussions. It also revises comparisons concerning K dependence while retaining the main positioning against context-discretization methods.

P1.justification: The title and CCV-MAB terminology change to 'changing action sets' and C3-MAB. Contributions are rewritten, application subsections and labeled remarks are added, and future directions become a separate subsection. The overall section sequence and most method and experimental prose remain.

P2.justification: Table 1’s caption and terminology are revised, figures and pseudocode shift within the document, and v2 adds running headers and page numbers. All seven figures retain their graphics; no empirical display is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The revised eigenvalue-based proof and explicit limitations provide useful theoretical clarification. However, unlike v1’s matching main-text and appendix kernel bounds, v2 states the RBF bound as sqrt(λ*(K)DKT) in Corollary 2 but λ*(K)sqrt(DKT) in Appendix A. Section 6 also omits the eigenvalue factor from the general regret claim. These inconsistencies concern the central revised contribution, leaving its benefits and losses in mathematical clarity without a reliably assessable net quality direction.
